title: An interrupted repeated relation either keeps one scope or closes before the intervening atom
summary: GDT575 records 62 interrupted same-root repeats such as relation–intervening atom–relation. The semantic law makes scope explicit: the second relation either resumes the first scope or starts a new scope.

design.mechanism: scope continuation across interruption versus local scope reset
design.contrast: For a held interrupted pair, a continuation model predicts one shared target/field across the intervening atom; a reset model predicts two independently licensed scopes and permits different targets.
design.prediction: Earlier repetition and A-B-A proposals treated recurrence or referent resumption, but did not make scope continuation versus reset the mutually exclusive semantic law.
design.countermodel: A renderer or position-conditioned convention can reproduce the observed layouts without the proposed semantic law.
design.falsifier: A single shared target is impossible while both relations remain licensed, or the same scope survives only after adding an unrecorded marker.
design.principal_risk: No independent target identities or scope markers are available; source order alone is insufficient.
design.smallest_test: Choose two interrupted pairs with complete surrounding fields and record whether one target constraint can satisfy both sides without renderer glosses.
design.prior_duplicate_pointers: Near IDEA000007/062 and GDT575; distinct target is scope state, not participant identity or boundary counting.
design.selection_status: raw unreviewed; no readiness or novelty claim
